content: Magnesium citrate is a laxative that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of constipation and magnesium deficiency. Common side effects associated with its use include diarrhea, weakness (asthenia), dizziness, and elevated magnesium levels in the blood (hypermagnesemia). For adults, magnesium citrate is indicated for the relief of occasional constipation. The recommended dosage is 5 to 10 fluid ounces within a 24-hour period. Each dose should be taken with a full glass (8 ounces) of liquid. It can be administered as a single daily dose or divided into multiple doses throughout the day. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium citrate in adults. For pediatric patients, magnesium citrate is also indicated for the relief of occasional constipation. It generally produces a bowel movement within 30 minutes to 6 hours. The dosage varies by age group: Children aged 6 to under 12 years: 3 to 7 fluid ounces, with a maximum of 7 fluid ounces in 24 hours. Children aged 2 to under 6 years: 2 to 3 fluid ounces. Children under 2 years: Consult a doctor. Each dose should be taken with a full glass (8 ounces) of liquid. It can be administered as a single daily dose or divided into multiple doses. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of magnesium citrate in pediatric patients. There is limited information available regarding contraindications, warnings, and adverse reactions from clinical trials for magnesium citrate. However, postmarketing data indicate that common gastrointestinal side effects include diarrhea. Neurological side effects such as weakness (asthenia) and dizziness have also been reported. Rare but serious side effects include hypermagnesemia (elevated magnesium levels) and hypoventilation (reduced breathing rate). Magnesium citrate has limited documented drug interactions. There is no specific FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, breastfeeding, or in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal-impaired, hepatic-impaired, or immunocompromised populations. Magnesium citrate is administered orally. There is limited information regarding its monitoring, intravenous compatibility, overdose management, pharmacology, mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, and clinical studies. If an overdose or poisoning is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline at 1-800-222-1222 immediately. There is no established interaction between alcohol and magnesium citrate. Patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication.
